1948, November 13
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O. F. M. Cap.
St. Felix Friary Route 8 Huntington, Indiana 1948, November 13
Bles'd be God in His each and every design.
Dear Mrs. and Mr. Turner:
God bless you, and keep you fostering the happy resignation in your souls which looms out in that little word of Mrs. Turner: "I have eased up on offering prayers for a complete cure; feeling that perhaps my constant inconvenience may help the poor Souls and also in the conversion of poor sinners." And then again: "God knows my needs, etc., etc.
That really sounds lile fostering confidence in God, than which hardly anything can be more pleasing to God and at the same time more profitable to our own poor souls. Such resign- ation and Confidence is a great grace in itself, which we should at all time and in all circumstances foster.
Your promotion of devotion to our dear Bl. Virgin Mother Mary by means of the rosary and the scapular will surely bring untold blessings on you and yours. By all means keep it up. for we can never be to grateful enough to such a singlarly chosen and privileged blessed Queen of the entire creation, God's own blessed Mother, whom, in His infinite condescention, wisdom and mercy has deigned to give to each and all of us if we only appreciate.
As to the stole proposition; well I do not remember or know of any one specially in need of such a prized garment jus off-hand now. I do know we have many priests on the Missions in Central America and in Islands who would surely appreciate such a donation. Probably the simplest solution would be to give the equivalent to some one in immediate touch with the mission-work going on in so many places. Our own Father Pro- vincial of course would know best where to place such a dona- tion. I am sure Brother Rufin or any one at the desk in St. Bonaventure's in Detroit would be able and pleased to receive the favor. Or if preferable you could include it sometime whenyou send a check hither to St. Felix.
